correctness.rationale: PASS. Each face splits uniquely into a matching B of original edges plus compatible pendant edges. On the augmented face poset, toggling the pendant edge at the least uncovered base vertex pairs every B not perfect; along a directed Morse path B cannot gain edges, and at fixed B the pivot cannot be deleted except along its matched arrow, excluding directed cycles. Unpaired faces are exactly the original perfect matchings, in dimension m-1. Removing the empty-face pair yields one critical 0-cell and |PM| critical (m-1)-cells, including n=2/m=1 as a wedge of 0-spheres. For each P, join of differences [b_e]-[w_v] is a reduced cycle. Endpoint switches are boundaries using [w_u]-[w_v], and maximal base-simplex coefficient cocycles pair as an integer identity matrix, proving primitive basis and automorphism sign on edge permutations. Independently enumerated all labeled base graphs on n<=4 (1,2,8,64 cases) and checked the complete augmented Morse DAG for every case; inspected full source checker of larger random examples and Lefschetz characters. Infinite universal proof is combinatorial, not an extrapolation.

The cited Singh 2021 source is specifically about complexes of forests; its use in submitted relationship-to-prior-work as a blanket fully-whiskered graph result appears overstated and should be verified/corrected before public distribution, although it does not undermine the independent proof of the central theorem.
